body.from: 3. Pick the runners. Use the `arena runners` line in `.pstack/models.md`. If `.pstack/models.md` or that line is missing, default to one each on `judgment-model` and `fast-code-model`. If dropped seats leave fewer than two runners, add runners until there are two, or one when the line has one entry. Run each added runner on a remaining runner's model, or omit `model` so it runs on the parent model when none remain, and say so. Spawn more runners when the arena covers multiple design directions. body.from: After all Phase B candidates complete, choose one model from the `arena cross-judge pool` line in `.pstack/models.md`. If `.pstack/models.md` or that line is missing, choose from `judgment-model` and `fast-code-model`. Spawn one read-only judge subagent. The judge is never from the parent's family, as Phase A step 3 defines families. Try only the entries from another family, in pool order. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry is the parent model, so it never judges. With the default pool, a Claude parent gets `fast-code-model`. A parent from any other family gets `judgment-model` first. If the host delegation capability rejects an entry, use a valid slug of the same model at the closest level or speed from the error message, or move to the next entry when there is none. If no entry from another family runs, try the default pool's entries from another family the same way. If none of those runs, skip the judge, pick the base alone in Phase D, and say so. If you do not know the parent's model, try the pool's real slugs in pool order and say that the family check did not run. The judge sees the rubric and the candidates by path label, scores each criterion, and recommends a base with rationale. It runs in parallel with your reading in Phase D. Don't spawn it while candidates are still writing.
body.to: After all Phase B candidates complete, choose one independent judge from the `arena cross-judge pool` line in `.pstack/models.md`; without a configured pool, use `auto`. # Main worktree is the first entry; everything else is a candidate.
main_wt=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')
scripts/worktree-audit.sh.to:
audit_tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$audit_tmp"' EXIT
if ! git worktree list --porcelain -z > "$audit_tmp/worktrees"; then
	echo "error: could not list worktrees" >&2
	exit 1
fi
main_wt=""
while IFS= read -r -d '' record; do
	case "$record" in 'worktree '*) main_wt=${record#worktree }; break ;; esac
done < "$audit_tmp/worktrees"
[ -n "$main_wt" ] || { echo "error: worktree list has no main worktree" >&2; exit 1; }

hold_error() {
	printf 'error: could not %s for %q\n' "$1" "$wt" >&2
	printf '?\t?\t?\terror\t?\t?\t?\thold-error\t%q\n' "$wt"
}

	if [ -z "$porcelain" ]; then dirty=clean
	elif printf '%s\n' "$porcelain" | grep -qv '^??'; then
		dirty="wip:$(printf '%s\n' "$porcelain" | grep -cv '^??')"
	else dirty="scratch:$(printf '%s\n' "$porcelain" | grep -c '^??')"; fi
scripts/worktree-audit.sh.to:
if ! git -C "$wt" status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=no > "$audit_tmp/tracked" 2>/dev/null; then
		hold_error "read tracked status"; continue
	fi
	if ! git -C "$wt" ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z > "$audit_tmp/untracked" 2>/dev/null; then
		hold_error "list untracked files"; continue
	fi
	if ! git -C "$wt" ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z > "$audit_tmp/ignored" 2>/dev/null; then
		hold_error "list ignored files"; continue
	fi
	if [ -s "$audit_tmp/tracked" ]; then dirty=wip
	elif [ -s "$audit_tmp/untracked" ] || [ -s "$audit_tmp/ignored" ]; then dirty=local-files
	else dirty=clean; fi

body.from: **Defaults for every delegation call.** `run concurrently when supported` (a steer or resume of a running agent too, because a foreground call holds your turn while other reports wait), the least privilege needed for its assigned reads or writes, file pointers not inlined context, explicit model per role (configurable via `setup-pstack`. Defaults `fast-code-model` for code, `judgment-model` for prose and judgment). Code delegates tier by difficulty. The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest judgment model (`judgment-model`), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model. Per-role lines in `.pstack/models.md`, which `setup-pstack` writes, override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent chat model (leave the model unset on the delegation call). Each code playbook's configured model comes from its line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), and the hardest changes read `hardest tasks`. Prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`.
body.to: **Defaults for every delegation call.** Run workers concurrently when supported, give each only the access its task needs, and provide file pointers and a clear brief. Use `auto` for every role unless `.pstack/models.md` supplies a model ID confirmed available in this session. `auto` and `inherit-parent` mean omit `model`. A role label such as `fast-code-model` or `judgment-model` describes the task; never pass it as an ID. The role lines written by `setup-pstack` may select confirmed models for code, prose, review, and verification.

body.from: **Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, start from the role's line or default and pick the reasoning level and speed the job needs. The `setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level, xhigh by default. Raise it one step, up to max, for the hardest or subtlest work. Lower it one step for judgment and two or more steps for routine work. Use fast mode only when the job is urgent, meaning CI or trunk is red or a person is blocked on the result right now. Otherwise use standard speed, the same slug without `-fast`. Verification is the exception and stays on the `swarm workers` model and speed (`fast-code-model` by default). Change only the effort level and whether the slug is fast, and keep the family the role names, so a diverse panel stays diverse. If the family has no slug at that level and speed, use its nearest slug. A role on `auto` or `inherit-parent` stays on the parent model. If the host delegation capability rejects the adjusted slug, do not try another adjusted slug. Use the role's line or default and say so. If the host delegation capability rejects that too, continue with the calling skill's fallback. A slug counts as rejected once a delegation operation error says that the model is not valid, or leaves the slug out of its list of valid slugs. Never pass a rejected slug, and skip any fallback whose slug is already rejected. When the calling skill has no fallback, use the closest valid slug of the role's family from the error's list of valid slugs, or omit `model` so the subagent runs on the parent model when the list has none. When the calling skill's fallback runs out of slugs without saying what to do next, omit `model` too. Say so in both cases.
body.to: **Match the model to the job.** Use the host's documented model, effort, and speed controls when available. Do not derive family, effort, or speed from a model ID's spelling. If a configured model is rejected, omit `model`, continue on the parent model, and say so. Never retry an ID the host rejected.

principle-attack-the-premise.description: Question a shared premise after two fixes built on it fail the same check.

principle-boundary-discipline.description: Place validation and error handling at external system boundaries.

principle-build-the-lever.description: Build reusable automation when a task benefits from repeatable edits or verification.

principle-encode-lessons-in-structure.description: Turn a recurring correction into an enforceable check or reusable mechanism.

principle-exhaust-the-design-space.description: Compare candidate designs for a novel interaction or architectural decision.

body.from: It also applies to product design decisions where user experience depends on feel, not logic.
body.to:
Use this procedure for a novel interaction or architectural choice with no established solution. It also applies to product design decisions where user experience depends on feel, not logic.

1. Set the comparison criteria before building the candidates. Use the user's goal and constraints.
2. Build two or three distinct prototypes. Compare different approaches, not cosmetic variations of one approach.
3. Compare the observed results against the same criteria. Record what each prototype proves and what remains untested.
4. Choose the strongest candidate. Give the reasons, tradeoffs, and evidence behind the choice.

Keep ordinary changes with an established solution outside this procedure.

principle-explain-the-number.description: Find what limits a measured number and rule out other causes before trusting or reporting it.

principle-make-operations-idempotent.description: Design retryable commands and processing loops to converge after partial execution.

principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-le.description: Plan caller migration and legacy removal when replacing an internal API.

principle-minimize-reader-load.description: Simplify code whose layers or hidden state make behavior hard to trace.

principle-model-the-domain.description: Represent domain states directly when scattered conditions obscure valid behavior.

principle-never-block-on-the-human.description: Resolve routine decisions within authorized reversible work.

principle-outcome-oriented-execution.description: Keep a planned rewrite or migration focused on its target architecture.

principle-prove-it-works.description: Verify the actual requested result before reporting completion.

principle-redesign-from-first-principles.description: Reconsider an existing design when a new requirement changes its assumptions.

principle-separate-before-serializing-sh.description: Reduce shared writes before adding serialization to concurrent work.

principle-sequence-verifiable-units.description: Sequence a migration or multi-step change into independently verifiable units.

principle-subtract-before-you-add.description: Identify removable code before expanding a refactor or feature.

principle-test-behavior-not-implementati.description: Test observable behavior through the code's public interface against literal expected values.

principle-type-system-discipline.description: Model valid states and checked external inputs in a static type system.
